method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Rotavirus' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- health.gov.au states 'all other rights are reserved'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **All infants: a course of oral rotavirus vaccine before 6 months**, the first dose **from as early as 6 weeks**.
claims.source_text: All infants are recommended to receive a course of oral rotavirus vaccine before they are 6 months old. Infants can receive the 1st dose of rotavirus vaccine as early as 6 weeks of age
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The course depends on the brand: Rotarix = 2 doses at 2 and 4 months; RotaTeq = 3 doses at 2, 4 and 6 months.**
claims.source_text: The vaccination course of Rotarix is 2 doses, at 2 and 4 months of age. The vaccination course of RotaTeq is 3 doses, at 2, 4 and 6 months of age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **There are strict upper age limits** — for Rotarix the limit for dose 2 is 24 weeks.
claims.source_text: upper age limit for dose 2 of 24 weeks.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Preterm infants: start at a chronological age of at least 6 weeks if clinically stable.**
claims.source_text: Preterm infants are recommended to receive either rotavirus vaccine starting at the chronological age of at least 6 weeks, if the infant is clinically stable.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Complete the full course even after rotavirus gastroenteritis — one infection gives only partial immunity.**
claims.source_text: Infants who develop rotavirus gastroenteritis before receiving the full course of rotavirus vaccine should still complete the full 2- or 3-dose schedule. One rotavirus infection only provides partial immunity.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rotavirus vaccination is associated with an increased risk of intussusception** — a form of bowel obstruction most often seen in young children.
claims.source_text: Intussusception is a form of bowel obstruction, most often seen in young children. Rotavirus vaccination is associated with an increased risk of intussusception .
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Contraindicated with a history of intussusception, a congenital abnormality predisposing to it, or severe combined immunodeficiency.**
claims.source_text: history of intussusception congenital abnormality that may predispose to intussusception severe combined immunodeficiency in infants
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No feeding restrictions** before or after either vaccine. **Infants in households with pregnant women can be vaccinated.**
claims.source_text: There are no restrictions on the infant's feeding before or after vaccination with either rotavirus vaccine. … Infants living in households with pregnant women can receive rotavirus vaccines.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vaccination significantly reduces rotavirus-specific and all-cause hospital presentations for gastroenteritis.**
claims.source_text: Rotavirus vaccination significantly reduces rotavirus-specific and all-cause hospital presentations for gastroenteritis.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Rotavirus', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/rotavirus, retrieved 2026-09-23
